title: Thomas Spinelly to Henry VIII, Brussels, 1 February 1517 (BL Cotton MS Galba B V ff. 40-41; DECODE R8416)

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Galba B V ff. 40-41 (DECODE R8416)

plaintext.source: No contemporary decipherment; the cipher sentence is summarised in Letters and Papers Henry VIII II no. 2862.

transcription.notes: Five lines on f. 40v; signs transcribed as look-alike Unicode characters.

system.summary: Monoalphabetic substitution with invented signs (Greek and Latin letters for other values), word division kept, plus word signs for of, this, that, the Emperor and probably the King.
system.notes: Five cipher lines inside a clear English despatch.

prior_solution.where: Letters and Papers Henry VIII II no. 2862 (1864) summarises the cipher sentence (Emperor to Cambrai about the 15th); no text printed

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the 4 DECODE images with the session cookie.
Read the pages: Spinelly autograph despatch to Henry VIII in clear English, Brussels 1 Feb 1516/17; cipher only in five lines on f. 40v.
Transcribed the 43 cipher tokens from zoomed crops.
Repeated 9-sign word with equal signs at positions 4 and 8 = audensier (spelled so in clear on the page); then and, the, to.
Extended the alphabet to the whole passage: Marliano, the King entry into Brussels, the Emperor to Cambrai about the xv day.
Letters and Papers Henry VIII II 2862 on British History Online: calendar summary of the cipher sentence only.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 156 tokens, 23 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.561 per letter; random keys -5.845 (z 5.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.455 (mean -3.608, z 10.4); annealer on the real text -3.13. Verdict: pass.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R8416 linked to transcription.txt and plaintext.txt; the key table copied verbatim from NOTES.md to texts/key.md
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.534; polyphony 0.013; 1 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.13

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The crib was the word 'audensier', spelled out in the clear English of the same page and repeated twice in the cipher as a 9-sign word with matching 4th and 8th signs; 'and', 'the' and 'to' followed and gave the whole alphabet.
outcome.notes: Alphabet certain; the word sign read as the King and sigma as l are probable. Agrees with the L&P summary.

texts.label: R8416, Cotton Galba B V f. 40v, Spinelly to Henry VIII, Brussels, 1 Feb 1517
texts.summary: The one cipher passage in Thomas Spinelly's clear despatch from the Low Countries: the Audiencier and Luigi Marliano (misser Loys de Merlien) report that the King (Charles) will make his entry into Brussels at the end of the week and that the Emperor Maximilian will go to Cambrai about the 15th of the month. Letters and Papers II 2862 had summarised only the Cambrai sentence.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 92.7% of the words of plaintext.txt read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
